rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: LLM never calls your Python tool (tools=[my_fn]), or asks how ADK builds the tool schema
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: ADK builds schema from function name, docstring (description), parameters, type hints, and default values (params without defaults = required). Model NEVER sees function body or # comments. No manual JSON schema.

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: Parent Coordinator/Orchestrator agent fails to delegate tasks to a specialist sub-agent
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: Sub-agent is missing a clear, specific name and description in Agent(name=..., description=...). Use workflow patterns when steps are predefined; use coordinator only when model must decide the route.

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: Need deterministic orchestration without paying an LLM call for routing, or mixing node types in ADK 2.0 graph
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: SequentialAgent / ParallelAgent / LoopAgent orchestrate deterministically with no model call. ADK 2.0 graphs support Functions, human input, Tools, LLM capabilities + Join nodes. Event.state is readable by any downstream node; output reaches ONLY the immediate next node.
rapidReflexTriggers.ref: Core Guide §1.2; M0L7 Slides 10–12; M3L1 Slide 9

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: Customer wants $0 compute cost when the agent sits idle overnight / on weekends
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: Deploy on Cloud Run (serverless container that scales to zero). Supply session service via --agent_engine_id (VertexAiSessionService) or DatabaseSessionService.

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: Customer wants managed durable sessions & Memory Bank out-of-the-box with zero infra management
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: Deploy on Agent Runtime (adk deploy agent_engine) — auto-creates VertexAiSessionService (loads/saves Session objects & applies state_delta). Real implementations: InMemorySessionService, DatabaseSessionService, VertexAiSessionService (watch out for fake TextEmbeddingService).
rapidReflexTriggers.ref: Core Guide §1.2; M0L9 Slides 7, 10, 13; M3L1 Slide 10

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: Workload needs custom networking, self-hosted open-source models not on Vertex AI, or full K8s control
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: Deploy on GKE — full control, custom networking, open models. Cost of control: 'you are the DevOps team'.

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: When to use Jetski (go/jetski) vs Antigravity 2.0 (agy)
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: Jetski = strictly internal productivity (google3, Buganizer, Critique) — NEVER show or screen-share with customers. Antigravity 2.0 (agy, Argolis auth) = safe for customer demos & 3P codebases.

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: What loads at startup for a skill, where do skills live, and what causes context failures?
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: Only name and description load at startup; full SKILL.md (description required, name optional + scripts/, examples/, resources/) loads when relevant or via /skill-name, solving 'tool bloat'. Project path: <project-root>/.agents/skills/<skill>/; Global: ~/.gemini/config/skills/. Failures: Observation flooding (raw logs) vs Context collapse (summarization drops fact) vs RAG grounding (company defs).
rapidReflexTriggers.ref: Core Guide §§1.1, 1.3; M1L1 Slides 8, 11; M1L2 Slide 13

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: 4 Phases of Google Cloud Migration Framework (in order) & AWS Lambda → Cloud Run advantage
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: 1. Assess -> 2. Plan & Build -> 3. Migrate -> 4. Optimize. Cloud Run advantage over Lambda: container-based (any language), up to 60-min timeout vs 15-min, concurrent requests per instance.

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: Users see a second sign-in prompt when querying Microsoft SharePoint via Gemini Enterprise Federated Connector
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: Not a misconfiguration! Federated connectors query Microsoft live with user-delegated permissions to enforce real-time SharePoint ACLs. Workforce Identity Federation (WIF) does NOT remove it.

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: Indirect Prompt Injection vs Tool Poisoning, and CodeMender with existing SAST tools
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: Indirect PI = malicious instructions inside content agent reads. Tool Poisoning = compromised MCP server/tool outputs. CodeMender is Stage 3 (Remediate) of Prepare -> Scan & Prioritize -> Remediate -> Monitor, supports 7 languages (C/C++, Go, Java, Python, Ruby, Rust, TypeScript), defaults to Gemini Flash (--model override), imports external SAST via 'cm report import' -> 'cm verify' -> 'cm fix'.
rapidReflexTriggers.ref: Core Guide §1.8; M2S1 Slides 44, 47–53; M2S2 Slide 5

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: Floor Settings, Confidence Levels, Rollout Sequence, SDP Basic vs Advanced, and 4 MB Limit
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: Floor settings = org/folder/project minimum. HIGH = fewest false positives; LOW_AND_ABOVE = strictest. Rollout: Inspect only -> tune -> Inspect and block. SDP Basic = predefined US infoTypes, flags only; Advanced = custom inspect template (required) + de-identify template (optional) for redaction/tokenization. >4 MB = skipped, not blocked, not billed. CSAM always on. Runs on any cloud/on-prem via REST API.

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: Agent Registry 3 goals, urn:agent:... vs principal://..., A2A vs standalone skills, Registry MCP tools
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: Goals: (1) Accelerate development, (2) Simplify integration, (3) Support governance. Identifier (urn:agent:...) = catalog lookup (never in IAM); Principal (principal://...) = SPIFFE/SA IAM identity. A2A skills = inline in Agent Card; Standalone skills = Skill, SkillRevision, Publisher. MCP tools: list_agents, search_agents, search_mcp_servers.

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: How Agent Registry separates Write vs Read operations, and auto vs manual registration
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: Automatic for supported GCP runtimes (Agent Runtime, Workspace/GE, annotated GKE, Google remote MCP servers) once API is enabled. Everything else (e.g., Cloud Run) is registered manually via writable Service resource, then queried via read-only Agent, McpServer, and Endpoint resources.

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: Agent calls BigQuery (GCP) AND a 3P SaaS API (Jira/ServiceNow) on user's behalf, governed by Agent Gateway
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: Dedicated SPIFFE X.509 identity per agent. BigQuery (GCP) uses agent's own identity (IAM). 3P SaaS uses user-delegated 3-legged OAuth via Agent Identity auth manager (token issued by SaaS OAuth server). Agent Gateway governs BOTH ingress and egress + Model Armor with NO app code changes.

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: Distinguish MCP vs A2A, A2A's 3 core technologies, and Agent Card URI
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: MCP = agent <-> tools/APIs/data. A2A = agent <-> agent peer collaboration, built on HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0, and Server-Sent Events (SSE). Agent Card URI: https://{server_domain}/.well-known/agent-card.json (RFC 8615; legacy /.well-known/agent.json).

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: How before_tool_callback ALLOWS vs BLOCKS a tool call, and how state prefixes work
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: Return None to ALLOW tool execution; return a dict to BLOCK/SHORT-CIRCUIT the tool and return that dict to the LLM. State scopes: unprefixed (session), user: (across sessions for user), app: (global across users), temp: (cleared after invocation).

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: Why passing unit tests / final-response evaluation isn't enough + 7 Coding Agent Eval Dimensions
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: Final-response eval misses 'right answer, wrong process'; Trajectory evaluation grades the reasoning path & tool call sequence. 7 Coding Eval Dimensions: Dim 1 = Intent Satisfaction, Dim 7 = Self-Repair Behaviour. Observability is the prerequisite.

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: Formula, Author, and Terminal Bench 2.0 empirical proof of Harness Engineering
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: Agent = Model + Harness (Vivek Trivedy, LangChain, Mar 2026; term coined by Mitchell Hashimoto, Feb 2026). On Terminal Bench 2.0, changing ONLY the harness jumped the same model from #30 (52.8%) to #5 (66.5%) (+13.7 pts).

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: What is inside a BigQuery ObjectRef, and what does MCP Toolbox for Databases handle?
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: ObjectRef is a STRUCT of uri, version, authorizer (Cloud resource connection), and details (content type, size, hash, updated)—does NOT cache bytes and is NOT a signed URL. MCP Toolbox for Databases handles connection pooling, IAM auth, and OTel observability in <10 lines of code.

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: What gen_ai.* attributes standardize, and the 4-level OTel hierarchy from SMALLEST to LARGEST
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: gen_ai.* attributes standardize BOTH names and semantic meanings across vendors. Hierarchy: 1. SPAN (atomic call) < 2. TRACE (1 turn) < 3. SESSION (multi-turn conversation) < 4. TASK (multi-agent workflow).

rapidReflexTriggers.trigger: Cache creation billing, Explicit vs Implicit storage cost, Min tokens, and Provisioned Throughput limits
rapidReflexTriggers.answer: Cache creation billed at standard input price for BOTH implicit and explicit. Explicit charges TTL storage; implicit has NO storage cost (~90% read discount on 2.5+). Min tokens: 2.5 Flash = 2,048; 3.x Flash = 4,096. Provisioned Throughput supports fine-tuned models, but NOT batch prediction and NOT other Agent Platform products (e.g., Agent Search).

tenMinuteSelfTest.q: What does an agent load at the start for each skill, and where do project skills live?
tenMinuteSelfTest.a: Only each skill's name and description (from SKILL.md YAML frontmatter); project skills live at <project-root>/.agents/skills/<skill>/ (global: ~/.gemini/config/skills/).

tenMinuteSelfTest.q: What makes a workflow agent different from an LLM agent?
tenMinuteSelfTest.a: A workflow agent (SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent, LoopAgent) runs sub-agents using predefined deterministic logic without consulting an AI model to orchestrate (no model call for routing).

tenMinuteSelfTest.q: What are Agent Registry's three goals, and which of its resources are writable versus read-only?
tenMinuteSelfTest.a: Goals: (1) Accelerate development, (2) Simplify integration, (3) Support governance. Writable: Service. Read-only: Agent, McpServer, Endpoint (plus Skill, SkillRevision, Publisher for standalone skills).

tenMinuteSelfTest.q: Which identity does an agent use for BigQuery versus a third-party SaaS app?
tenMinuteSelfTest.a: BigQuery (GCP resource): the agent's own SPIFFE identity (governed by IAM). Third-party SaaS on user's behalf: user-delegated 3-legged OAuth via Agent Identity auth manager (token issued by SaaS OAuth server).

tenMinuteSelfTest.q: What's the Model Armor rollout sequence, and what happens to a file over 4 MB?
tenMinuteSelfTest.a: Start in Inspect only, tune with test data/monitoring/feedback, then switch to Inspect and block. Files/text over 4 MB are skipped, not blocked, and not billed.

tenMinuteSelfTest.q: Which stage of AI Threat Defense does CodeMender's fix belong to?
tenMinuteSelfTest.a: Remediate (Stage 3 of Prepare -> Scan and Prioritize -> Remediate -> Monitor).

tenMinuteSelfTest.q: Who pays storage costs, explicit or implicit caching?
tenMinuteSelfTest.a: Explicit caching pays TTL storage costs; implicit caching has no storage cost (both pay standard input token price for cache creation).

tenMinuteSelfTest.q: Where is an A2A Agent Card hosted, and what three technologies is A2A built on?
tenMinuteSelfTest.a: Hosted at https://{server_domain}/.well-known/agent-card.json (RFC 8615; older versions used /.well-known/agent.json); built on HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0, and Server-Sent Events (SSE).

questions.q: A platform team wants every Model Armor template in the company to at least enable prompt-injection detection, while teams can still add stricter filters. What should they use?
options: Floor settings, which set minimum requirements at the org, folder, or project level that templates can't go below
One shared 'golden' template that every team must voluntarily reference
A confidence level of LOW_AND_ABOVE enforced via IAM Conditions
An IAM deny policy on the Model Armor API

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor | Trigger #12 | M2S2 Slide 44
questions.q: A customer complains that Model Armor blocks too many legitimate prompts. Which confidence level gives the FEWEST false positives?
options: HIGH (flags only high-likelihood violations, minimizing false positives)
LOW_AND_ABOVE (strictest setting, flags low, medium, and high)
MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE
Confidence level does not affect false-positive rates
questions.why: HIGH flags only high-confidence violations, resulting in the fewest false positives. LOW_AND_ABOVE is the strictest threshold and produces the most false positives.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor | Self-Test #5 & Trigger #12 | M2S2 Slide 49
questions.q: What is the recommended rollout sequence for a new Model Armor deployment?
options: Start in Inspect only, tune with test data, production monitoring, and user feedback, then switch to Inspect and block
Deploy straight to Inspect and block from day one, then relax filters if users complain
Keep Inspect only permanently, because blocking breaks LLM applications
Use Inspect and block for prompts and Inspect only for responses permanently
questions.why: Official best practice: start in Inspect only (logs findings without blocking), tune thresholds using test data, production telemetry, and feedback, and then switch to Inspect and block.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor | Trigger #12 (Swapped-Definition Trap) | M2S2 Slide 46
questions.q: A healthcare customer needs credit card numbers REDACTED or tokenized before prompts reach the model. What configuration do they need?
options: Advanced Sensitive Data Protection (SDP) configuration with an inspect template (required) and a de-identify template (optional)
Basic Sensitive Data Protection configuration (which automatically redacts US infoTypes)
The prompt-injection and jailbreak filter set to HIGH
A Responsible AI filter for 'dangerous content'
questions.why: Basic SDP uses a fixed set of predefined (mostly US) infoTypes and ONLY flags findings. Redaction or tokenization requires Advanced SDP with your own SDP inspect template (required) and de-identify template.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor | Self-Test #5 & Trigger #12 | M2S2 Slide 48
questions.q: A user uploads a 6 MB document for screening. What does Model Armor do?
options: Skips it (it isn't blocked), and the skipped data isn't billed
Blocks the file immediately because it exceeds the 4 MB limit
Compresses the file under 4 MB and then screens it
Splits the document into 4 MB chunks and screens each chunk
questions.why: Files and text over 4 MB are skipped (not blocked), and skipped data is not billed. Watch out for distractors claiming oversized files are blocked, compressed, or split.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor | Trigger #12 | M2S2 Slide 39

Only if routed through GKE Enterprise on Google Cloud
Only for batch prediction workloads stored in BigQuery

The first 10 URLs

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.7 Model Armor | Trigger #12 | M2S2 Slides 49–50
questions.q: A CE is configuring Model Armor for a customer for the first time. Which starting configuration matches Google's recommended phased strategy?
options: Responsible AI filters at HIGH, prompt injection at MEDIUM (or HIGH for Gemini Enterprise), advanced SDP templates, in Inspect only mode
Responsible AI at LOW_AND_ABOVE, prompt injection at HIGH, basic SDP, in Inspect and block mode
All filters at LOW_AND_ABOVE with Inspect and block enabled on day one
Responsible AI disabled, CSAM disabled, and Inspect only mode

Supports any image format up to 20 MB across all global regions
Scans up to 10 images per request for batch throughput
Only inspects EXIF image metadata, not visual text content

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Trigger #13 | M2S2 Slide 15
questions.q: What is Google Cloud Agent Registry?
options: A centralized catalog that lets you store, discover, and govern MCP servers, tools, standalone skills, and AI agents within Google Cloud
A managed serverless container runtime that replaces Cloud Run for ADK agents
A foundation model weight repository that replaces Vertex AI Model Registry
An API gateway that terminates mTLS and bills token usage
questions.why: Verbatim doc definition (§1.4): Agent Registry is 'a centralized catalog that lets you store, discover, and govern MCP servers, tools, standalone skills, and AI agents within Google Cloud.' It is not a runtime or model registry.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Self-Test #3 & Trigger #13 | M2S2 Slide 15
questions.q: What are the three official goals of Google Cloud Agent Registry?
options: Accelerate development, simplify integration, and support governance
Host containers, fine-tune foundation models, and manage token billing
Replace Cloud IAM, encrypt VPC traffic, and redact PII
Auto-scale runtimes, cache prompts, and provision throughput
questions.why: Agent Registry's three goals (§1.4) are: (1) Accelerate development (discovery and reuse), (2) Simplify integration (standardized MCP and A2A protocols), and (3) Support governance (enforce security and boundaries across the agentic fleet).

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Trigger #14 | M2S2 Slide 16
questions.q: A team deploys agents across Google Cloud. Which deployment requires MANUAL registration in Agent Registry via a writable Service resource?
options: An ADK A2A agent deployed on Cloud Run
An agent deployed on Agent Runtime (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform)
A GKE deployment configured with Agent Registry annotations
An official Google Cloud remote MCP server
questions.why: Auto-registration covers supported Google Cloud runtimes once the API is enabled (Agent Runtime, Workspace/Gemini Enterprise, annotated GKE, and official Google remote MCP servers). Cloud Run agents are NOT auto-discovered and require manual registration via the writable Service resource.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Self-Test #3 & Trigger #14 | M2S2 Slide 20
questions.q: When manually registering or updating an item in Agent Registry, which resource is WRITABLE versus READ-ONLY?
options: Service is writable; Agent, McpServer, and Endpoint are read-only
Agent and McpServer are writable; Service is read-only
Endpoint is writable; Service and Agent are read-only
All resources (Service, Agent, McpServer, Endpoint) are directly writable
questions.why: Everything registered manually is written through the writable 'Service' resource, and then queried through the read-only 'Agent', 'McpServer', and 'Endpoint' resources.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Trigger #13 (Swapped-Definition Trap) | M2S2 Slide 18
questions.q: A security engineer wants to grant an agent IAM permission to query BigQuery. Should they use the Agent Identifier or the Agent Principal?
options: Agent Principal (principal://...), because Agent Identifier (urn:agent:...) is only a logical catalog name and is never used in IAM bindings
Agent Identifier (urn:agent:...), because it is the primary IAM identity for all registered agents
Either one, because Identifier and Principal are interchangeable in IAM bindings
Neither, because agents can never hold an IAM identity for Google Cloud resources
questions.why: Agent Identifier (urn:agent:...) is a logical catalog ID used for inventory and lookup—never in IAM bindings. Agent Principal (principal://...) is the SPIFFE/service-account IAM identity used for permissions and auditing.

A2A skills are for MCP servers only; standalone skills are for Cloud Run only
There is no difference; both are stored exclusively inside an Agent Card
questions.why: A2A skills are declarative metadata declared inline in an agent's Agent Card. Standalone skills are separate catalog resources managed, versioned, and listed through the Skill, SkillRevision, and Publisher resources.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills | Self-Test #1 & Trigger #8 | M1L1 Slide 8
questions.q: What does an agent load into context at startup for each available Agent Skill?
options: Only each skill's name and description; the full SKILL.md is read only when the agent judges the skill relevant
The entire SKILL.md file for every installed skill
All files inside scripts/, examples/, and resources/ up front
Nothing at all until the user explicitly types a slash command
questions.why: Agent Skills use progressive disclosure: only each skill's name and description load at startup. The full SKILL.md is read only when the agent judges the skill relevant.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills | Trigger #8 | M1L1 Slide 6
questions.q: Which core problem are Agent Skills and progressive disclosure designed to solve?
options: Tool bloat, where loading hundreds of tools and rules into context makes the agent slower, costlier, and worse at picking the right one
Network latency between Cloud Run and BigQuery
Lack of encryption in third-party OAuth tokens
Container cold starts on GKE Autopilot
questions.why: Skills solve 'tool bloat'—where loading too many tools and instructions up front overwhelms the context window, increasing latency/cost and degrading tool selection accuracy.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills | Self-Test #1 & Trigger #8 | M1L1 Slide 11
questions.q: Where should a team store a PROJECT-SPECIFIC (workspace) skill so it is version-controlled and shared with the repo?
options: <project-root>/.agents/skills/<skill>/
~/.gemini/config/skills/<skill>/
/etc/google/skills/<skill>/
<project-root>/.well-known/skills/
questions.why: Project-specific (workspace) skills live at <project-root>/.agents/skills/<skill>/. Watch out for the trap offering ~/.gemini/config/skills/, which is the global path.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills | Self-Test #1 & Trigger #8 | M1L1 Slide 11
questions.q: A developer wants a custom skill to be available globally across all projects in Antigravity, the IDE, and the CLI. Where should they place it?
options: ~/.gemini/config/skills/
<project-root>/.agents/skills/
~/.config/gcloud/skills/
/usr/local/share/adk/skills/
questions.why: Global skills live at ~/.gemini/config/skills/ and work across Antigravity, the IDE, and the CLI.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills | Trigger #8 | M1L1 Slide 9
questions.q: In a skill's required SKILL.md YAML frontmatter, which field is REQUIRED and which is OPTIONAL?
options: description is required; name is optional
name is required; description is optional
Both name and version are required; description is optional
No YAML frontmatter is used in SKILL.md
questions.why: In SKILL.md YAML frontmatter, 'description' is required (since the agent uses it to judge relevance), and 'name' is optional.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills | Trigger #8 | M1L1 Slide 9
questions.q: Besides the required SKILL.md file, what optional subdirectories can an Agent Skill folder contain?
options: scripts/, examples/, and resources/
Nothing else; a skill folder can never contain anything but SKILL.md
Only compiled Docker images
Only Terraform state files
questions.why: A skill folder contains SKILL.md (required) plus optional scripts/, examples/, and resources/ directories.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills | Trigger #8 | M1L1 Slide 10
questions.q: How can an Agent Skill be activated during a session?
options: Automatically when the prompt's intent matches the skill's description, or explicitly with a slash command (/skill-name)
Only when the user explicitly types a slash command (/skill-name)
Only by restarting the agent container with a --skill flag
Only through a Cloud Scheduler cron job
questions.why: Skills activate either automatically (when the prompt's intent matches the skill's description) or explicitly via a slash command (/skill-name).

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 Agent Skills | Trigger #8 | M1L1 Slides 8–9
questions.q: An agent never automatically activates a newly created skill even when the user asks a relevant question. What is the most likely cause?
options: The skill's description in SKILL.md frontmatter is vague or missing the trigger keywords for that task
The user did not type the /skill-name slash command, which is mandatory for all skills
The optional scripts/ directory is empty
The skill was placed in <project-root>/.agents/skills/ instead of /tmp/
questions.why: Because the agent only sees each skill's name and description at startup, automatic activation relies on matching the prompt's intent to the YAML frontmatter description.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.1 & §6.6 | M1L1 Slide 7
questions.q: Which of the following correctly lists the 5 official Agent Skill design patterns from Module 1?
options: Informational, Tool Wrapper, Generator, Reviewer, and Workflow
Sequential, Parallel, Loop, Coordinator, and Router
Prepare, Scan, Remediate, Monitor, and Audit
Span, Trace, Session, Task, and Metric
questions.why: Per §6.6 (M1L1 Slide 7), the 5 Skill Patterns are: Informational (context for an environment/task), Tool Wrapper (how to use an existing tool/CLI), Generator (content of a specific format), Reviewer (criteria to assess work), and Workflow (repeatable multi-step sequence).

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.4 Agent Registry | Trigger #13 | M2S2 Slide 19
questions.q: When a standalone skill is registered in Agent Registry, how are updates to its instructions or code versioned?
options: Through an immutable SkillRevision resource under the parent Skill and Publisher resources
By overwriting the inline Agent Card JSON file on Cloud Run
By creating a new GCP project for every version
Standalone skills cannot be versioned once created
questions.why: Standalone skills are managed, versioned, and listed through the Skill, SkillRevision, and Publisher resources in Agent Registry.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 ADK Fundamentals | Self-Test #2 & Trigger #3 | M0L7 Slides 10–12
questions.q: How do ADK workflow agents (SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent, LoopAgent) orchestrate their sub-agents?
options: Using predefined deterministic logic without consulting an AI model to orchestrate (while sub-agents can still be LLM agents and call tools)
By calling an LLM router before every step to decide which sub-agent runs next
By prohibiting sub-agents from using an LLM or calling any tools
By converting all sub-agents into static SQL queries
questions.why: Workflow agents (SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent, LoopAgent) run sub-agents using predefined logic (in order, concurrently, or repeated) without consulting an AI model to orchestrate. Sub-agents can still be LLM agents and call tools.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 ADK Fundamentals | Trigger #2 | M0L7 Slide 25
questions.q: A team is building a pipeline where three steps always run in the exact same order and no model is needed to decide the route. Which design pattern should they choose?
options: A deterministic workflow pattern (such as SequentialAgent)
An LLM coordinator pattern, because every routing decision requires a model call
A standalone SkillRevision resource without ADK
An unauthenticated webhook loop
questions.why: Google's design guidance (§1.2): if the steps are predefined and no model needs to orchestrate them, use a deterministic workflow pattern. Use agentic patterns (coordinator) only when the model must decide the route.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 ADK Fundamentals | Trigger #1 | M0L6 Slides 6–7
questions.q: When you pass a Python function as an ADK tool, how does ADK build the tool schema that the model sees?
options: From the function's name, docstring, parameters, type hints, and default values
By reading the full Python function body and inline # comments
From a hand-written JSON schema file that you must author manually for every tool
From the function's return statement only
questions.why: ADK builds the tool schema from the function's name, docstring (becomes description), parameters, type hints, and default values. You never hand-write JSON schemas for function tools.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 ADK Fundamentals | Trigger #1 | M0L6 Slides 6–7
questions.q: In an ADK Python function tool, which parameters are treated as REQUIRED, and what does the model NEVER see?
options: Parameters without default values are required, and the model never sees the function body or # comments
Parameters with default values are required, and the model reads inline # comments for hints
All parameters are optional, and the model inspects the entire Python function body
Only string parameters are required, and the model ignores the docstring
questions.why: Parameters without default values are marked required in the tool schema; the docstring becomes the tool description; the model never sees the function body or # comments.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 ADK Fundamentals | Trigger #3 | M3L1 Slide 9
questions.q: Which node types are supported in an ADK 2.0 graph workflow, and how are parallel branches merged?
options: Functions, human input, Tools, and LLM capabilities (agents), with Join nodes merging parallel branches
LLM agent nodes only; graphs cannot include plain functions or human input
Tools and SQL nodes only, merged by a LoopAgent
Only Model Armor templates and Service resources
questions.why: ADK 2.0 graphs support four node types: Functions, human input, Tools, and LLM capabilities (agents), and use Join nodes to merge parallel branches.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 ADK Fundamentals | Trigger #3 | M3L1 Slide 9
questions.q: In an ADK 2.0 graph, what is the difference between setting data on an Event's 'state' field versus using 'output'?
options: Setting an Event's 'state' field lets any downstream node read it, whereas 'output' passes data only to the immediate next node
'output' is readable by all downstream nodes, whereas 'state' only reaches the immediate next node
Both 'state' and 'output' pass data only to the immediate next node
Neither 'state' nor 'output' can pass data between graph nodes
questions.why: Nodes set shared state through an Event's 'state' field so any downstream node can read it. 'output' passes data only to the immediate next node.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 ADK Fundamentals | Trigger #5 | M3L1 Slide 10
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a real ADK SessionService implementation (a classic exam distractor)?
options: TextEmbeddingService
InMemorySessionService
DatabaseSessionService
VertexAiSessionService
questions.why: The three real SessionService implementations are InMemorySessionService, DatabaseSessionService, and VertexAiSessionService. 'TextEmbeddingService' is a classic made-up distractor called out in §1.2.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 ADK Fundamentals | Trigger #5 | M3L1 Slide 10
questions.q: What does ADK's SessionService do during a conversation?
options: Loads and saves Session objects (one conversation's state and event history) and applies 'state_delta' from each event
Generates vector embeddings for PDF files stored in Cloud Storage
Builds the tool schema from Python docstrings and type hints
Issues 3-legged OAuth tokens for third-party SaaS applications
questions.why: SessionService loads and saves Session objects (state and event history) and applies the 'state_delta' from each event.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 & §5 Trigger #2 | M0L7 Slides 15–16
questions.q: A parent Coordinator LLM agent fails to delegate tasks to a specialist sub-agent. What is the most likely fix in ADK?
options: Give the sub-agent a clear, specific 'name' and 'description' in Agent(name=..., description=...)
Rewrite the sub-agent as a C++ binary
Remove the docstring from all Python function tools
Switch from VertexAiSessionService to TextEmbeddingService
questions.why: Per Trigger #2, when an LLM coordinator fails to route to a specialist sub-agent, the sub-agent is missing a clear, specific 'name' and 'description' in Agent(name=..., description=...).

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §5 Trigger #17 | M3L1 Slides 14–19
questions.q: In ADK's before_tool_callback, what happens when the callback returns None versus returning a dict?
options: Returning None allows normal tool execution; returning a dict blocks/short-circuits the tool and returns that dict to the LLM
Returning None blocks the tool call; returning a dict allows normal execution
Returning a dict deletes the current session state
Both None and dict skip the tool call and terminate the agent
questions.why: Per Trigger #17: In before_tool_callback, return None to ALLOW normal tool execution; return a dict to BLOCK/SHORT-CIRCUIT the tool and return that dict directly to the LLM.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §5 Trigger #17 | M3L1 Slide 10
questions.q: An ADK developer wants to store a user's preferred language in session state so it persists across multiple conversation sessions for that specific user. Which state prefix should they use?
options: user: (e.g., state['user:preferred_language'])
temp: (cleared after the current invocation)
app: (shared globally across all users of the application)
No prefix (persists only within the single current session)
questions.why: Per Trigger #17: ADK has 4 state scopes: unprefixed (current session only), 'user:' (persists across sessions for that specific user), 'app:' (global across all users), and 'temp:' (cleared after the current invocation).

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §5 Trigger #17 | M3L1 Slide 10
questions.q: In ADK state management, what happens to keys written with the 'temp:' prefix (such as state['temp:scratch_data'])?
options: They exist only during the current invocation (turn) and are automatically cleared when the turn finishes
They persist permanently across all users in VertexAiSessionService
They are automatically exported to BigQuery after 60 minutes
They cause the SessionService to reset the user's conversation history
questions.why: The 'temp:' prefix is for temporary scratch data needed only within the current invocation; ADK clears 'temp:' keys once the invocation completes.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 & Tab 3 M0L7 Slides 10–12
questions.q: In a SequentialAgent pipeline, Agent 1 summarizes a report and Agent 2 needs to read that summary in its system instruction. What is the standard ADK pattern?
options: Set output_key='summary' on Agent 1, and reference '{summary}' in Agent 2's instruction
Have Agent 1 write to a local file in /tmp and have Agent 2 call a bash tool
Set include_contents='none' on both agents
Pass Agent 1 inside Agent 2's generate_content_config
questions.why: Setting output_key='summary' saves Agent 1's final response to session.state['summary'], and Agent 2 automatically injects it into its prompt via the '{summary}' placeholder.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 & Tab 3 M0L7 Slide 11
questions.q: Two sub-agents inside a ParallelAgent run concurrently and save their outputs to session state. How should you prevent them from overwriting each other?
options: Configure a distinct output_key on each sub-agent (e.g., output_key='data_a' and output_key='data_b')
Configure the exact same output_key on both sub-agents so ADK merges them
Disable SessionService when running ParallelAgent
Set max_iterations=1 on the ParallelAgent
questions.why: Sub-agents in a ParallelAgent execute concurrently against the same session.state, so each branch must write to a distinct output_key to avoid race conditions.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 & Tab 3 M0L7 Slide 12
questions.q: How does a sub-agent or tool stop an ADK LoopAgent early before it hits max_iterations?
options: Emit an Event with EventActions(escalate=True) (or set tool_context.actions.escalate = True)
Return None from the LLM prompt
Raise a Python RuntimeError inside the tool
Set disallow_transfer_to_parent=True
questions.why: LoopAgent repeats its sub-agents until either max_iterations is reached or a sub-agent/tool emits an event with escalate=True.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 & Tab 3 M0L7 Slides 15–18
questions.q: What is the difference between wrapping a specialist agent in AgentTool(specialist) versus adding it to sub_agents=[specialist]?
options: With AgentTool, the parent invokes the specialist like a tool and stays in control; with sub_agents, the parent transfers conversation control to the specialist
With sub_agents, the parent stays in control; with AgentTool, the specialist takes over the conversation permanently
AgentTool only works on GKE, whereas sub_agents only works on Cloud Run
There is no difference; both permanently hand off control to the specialist
questions.why: AgentTool wraps an agent as a callable tool so its answer returns to the parent agent (which stays in control). Listing it in sub_agents delegates/transfers control of the turn.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — Tab 2 M3L1 & Tab 3 M0L6
questions.q: What important limitation applies when you configure output_schema (a Pydantic model) on an ADK LlmAgent?
options: Using output_schema disables tool calling and sub-agent delegation for that agent
Using output_schema disables VertexAiSessionService
Using output_schema requires hand-writing a toolspec.json file
output_schema is only supported on third-party models via LiteLLM
questions.why: In ADK, setting output_schema on an LlmAgent enforces structured JSON output, which disables tool calling and sub-agent delegation for that specific agent.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §5 Trigger #17 | M3L1 Slides 14–19
questions.q: A developer uses before_model_callback as a guardrail to block disallowed prompts before calling Gemini. What should the callback return?
options: Return an LlmResponse object to skip the model call (or return None to allow the model call to proceed)
Return None to block the model call, and return True to allow it
Return a numeric HTTP status code like 403
before_model_callback can only log prompts and cannot skip the model call
questions.why: In before_model_callback, returning None allows the LLM request to proceed normally, whereas returning an LlmResponse object short-circuits the LLM call and returns that response directly.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §5 Triggers #4, #5 & #6 | M0L9 Slides 6–15
questions.q: A customer wants zero compute cost ($0) when their ADK agent sits idle overnight and on weekends. Which runtime should they choose?
options: Cloud Run, because it scales to zero when idle (while Agent Runtime is best when they want turnkey managed sessions and Memory Bank)
GKE with always-on dedicated node pools
BigQuery Provisioned Throughput
Vertex AI Model Registry
questions.why: Per Triggers #4–#6: Choose Cloud Run when the requirement is '$0 compute cost while idle' (scales to zero). Choose Agent Runtime for turnkey managed sessions (VertexAiSessionService) and Memory Bank. Choose GKE for custom networking or self-hosted open models.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §5 Trigger #7 | M0L5 Slides 6–8
questions.q: A Google Cloud CE is preparing a live customer screen-share demo of an agentic workflow on a 3P codebase. Should they use Jetski or Antigravity 2.0 (agy)?
options: Antigravity 2.0 (agy), because Jetski is strictly internal-only (google3/Buganizer/Critique) and must NEVER be shown or screen-shared with customers
Jetski, because it is Google's external customer-facing IDE
Either tool, because both are approved for external customer screen-sharing
Neither; live demos can only be run inside HackerRank Secure Mode
questions.why: Per Trigger #7 (M0L5 Slides 6–8): Jetski is exclusively for internal productivity (google3, Buganizer, Critique) and must NEVER be shown to customers. Antigravity 2.0 (agy, authenticated via Argolis) is safe for customer-facing demos and 3P codebases.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway | Trigger #15 | M2S2 Slide 24
questions.q: What type of cryptographic identity does Google Cloud Agent Identity assign to each agent?
options: A dedicated SPIFFE-based identity with an X.509 certificate that is not shared and cannot be impersonated
A shared default Compute Engine service account JSON key
A static API key stored in an environment variable
A browser session cookie shared across all agents in the project
questions.why: Each agent gets its own SPIFFE-based identity with an X.509 certificate assigned by Google Cloud. It is not shared and cannot be impersonated.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway | Self-Test #4 & Trigger #15 | M2S2 Slide 25
questions.q: When an agent queries a Google Cloud resource like BigQuery, which identity does it use?
options: The agent's own SPIFFE identity, governed by Google Cloud IAM
A 3-legged OAuth token issued by an external SaaS server
Its logical Agent Registry Identifier (urn:agent:...)
Agents never hold their own credential and must use an anonymous key
questions.why: For Google Cloud resources (like BigQuery), the agent uses its own SPIFFE identity governed by IAM. Watch out for the wrong option claiming 'an agent never holds its own credential.'

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway | Self-Test #4 & Trigger #15 | M2S2 Slide 26
questions.q: An agent needs to create a Jira ticket in a third-party SaaS app on the user's behalf. How does it authenticate?
options: User-delegated 3-legged OAuth through the Agent Identity auth manager
The agent's own Google Cloud IAM service account
Hardcoding the user's credentials in the system prompt
Using an IAM deny policy on the BigQuery API
questions.why: When calling a third-party SaaS app on the user's behalf, the agent uses user-delegated 3-legged OAuth through the Agent Identity auth manager.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway | Trigger #15 | M2S2 Slide 26
questions.q: When an agent uses 3-legged OAuth via the Agent Identity auth manager to call a third-party SaaS API, who issues the access token?
options: The third-party SaaS OAuth server
Google Cloud IAM
Model Armor
BigQuery
questions.why: In user-delegated 3-legged OAuth for a third-party SaaS app, the token is issued by the SaaS OAuth server and managed by the Agent Identity auth manager.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway | Self-Test #4 & Trigger #15 | M2S2 Slides 25–26
questions.q: In one workflow, an agent reads data from BigQuery and then updates a ticket in ServiceNow on the user's behalf. Which credentials does it use?
options: Its own SPIFFE identity (IAM) for BigQuery, and user-delegated 3-legged OAuth for ServiceNow
One combined credential that authenticates to both BigQuery and ServiceNow
User-delegated 3-legged OAuth for both BigQuery and ServiceNow
Its SPIFFE identity for ServiceNow, and 3-legged OAuth for BigQuery
questions.why: Classic §1.5 scenario: the agent uses its own SPIFFE identity (governed by IAM) for GCP resources like BigQuery, and user-delegated 3-legged OAuth for third-party SaaS apps.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway | Trigger #15 | M2S2 Slide 28
questions.q: Which traffic directions does Google Cloud Agent Gateway govern?
options: Both ingress (inbound to the agent) and egress (outbound from the agent to tools and other agents)
Egress traffic only
Ingress traffic only
Neither; Agent Gateway only handles token billing
questions.why: Agent Gateway governs both ingress and egress traffic and enforces access policies. Watch out for traps saying it 'only handles egress' or 'only billing.'

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway | Trigger #15 | M2S2 Slide 28
questions.q: A security team configures Agent Gateway with Model Armor to inspect an agent's tool calls and responses. What application code changes are required?
options: No application code changes are needed
Every tool function must be rewritten to call the Model Armor REST API manually
The agent must be migrated from Python to Go
Every prompt must be manually encrypted inside the agent code
questions.why: Agent Gateway is a fully managed component that governs ingress/egress traffic, enforces access policies, and integrates with Model Armor to inspect tool calls and responses with no app code changes needed.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 Agent Identity & Gateway | Trigger #15 | M2S2 Slides 24–29
questions.q: Which statement accurately describes the relationship between Agent Gateway and Agent Identity?
options: Agent Gateway works alongside and requires Agent Identity; it does not replace Agent Identity
Agent Gateway replaces Agent Identity so agents no longer need SPIFFE certificates
Agent Gateway and Agent Identity cannot be used together
Agent Gateway is a container runtime that replaces Cloud Run and GKE
questions.why: Watch out for the trap 'Gateway replaces Agent Identity.' Agent Gateway is a managed ingress/egress control point that works alongside Agent Identity.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 & Tab 2 M2S2 Slide 25
questions.q: When deploying an agent to Agent Runtime, when can Agent Identity (--agent-identity) be enabled?
options: Only when the agent is created
Only after the agent is deleted
Automatically whenever a file over 4 MB is uploaded
Only on third-party on-premises servers
questions.why: On Agent Runtime, Agent Identity (--agent-identity) is immutable after creation and can only be enabled when the agent is first created.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.5 & Tab 2 M2S2 Slide 29
questions.q: Why must a container image trust AGENT_GATEWAY_ROOT_CERTIFICATES when bound to an egress Agent Gateway?
options: Because an egress Agent Gateway performs TLS decryption and inspection on outbound agent traffic
Because BigQuery requires client-side TLS certificates for SQL syntax parsing
Because Agent Registry stores skill files inside X.509 certificates
Because OAuth tokens are compiled into the Dockerfile at build time
questions.why: An egress Agent Gateway performs TLS inspection (with Model Armor) on outbound communications, so the container image must trust the gateway's root CA.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.6 Protocols (Swapped-Definition Trap) | Trigger #16 | M3L1 Slide 31
questions.q: What is the fundamental architectural difference between Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent2Agent (A2A)?
options: MCP connects an agent to its tools, APIs, and data sources; A2A enables independent agents to discover each other and collaborate as peers
A2A connects an agent to databases and tools; MCP enables peer-to-peer delegation between autonomous agents
MCP is only for on-premises servers, while A2A is only for BigQuery SQL queries
MCP and A2A are identical protocols with different marketing names
questions.why: Watch out for the classic swapped-definition trap (§1.6): MCP = agent ↔ tools, APIs, and data sources. A2A = agent ↔ agent (peer discovery and collaboration to delegate work).

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.6 Protocols | Self-Test #8 & Trigger #16 | M3L1 Slide 31
questions.q: Which three core web technologies is the A2A protocol built on?
options: HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0, and Server-Sent Events (SSE)
WebSockets, GraphQL, and WebRTC
MQTT, Protobuf binary framing, and FTP
SOAP XML, CORBA, and Raw TCP sockets
questions.why: Per Self-Test #8 and §1.6: A2A reuses existing web standards—specifically HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0, and Server-Sent Events (SSE). Avoid exotic stack distractors like WebSockets/GraphQL/WebRTC or MQTT.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.6 Protocols | Self-Test #8 & Trigger #16 | M3L1 Slide 32
questions.q: Where is an A2A Agent Card hosted according to the RFC 8615 well-known URI standard?
options: https://{server_domain}/.well-known/agent-card.json (older versions used /.well-known/agent.json)
https://{server_domain}/api/v1/skills/SKILL.md
~/.gemini/config/skills/agent-card.yaml
urn:agent:google:agent-card
questions.why: Per §1.6 & Self-Test #8: An A2A Agent Card is published at https://{server_domain}/.well-known/agent-card.json following RFC 8615 well-known URIs (older versions used /.well-known/agent.json).

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.6 Protocols | Trigger #20 | M3L4 Slide 20
questions.q: What does Google's open-source MCP Toolbox for Databases handle for developers out of the box?
options: Connection pooling, authentication (IAM), and OpenTelemetry observability, allowing database tools to be added to an agent in under 10 lines of code
Training custom foundation models directly inside Cloud SQL stored procedures
Replacing Agent Registry with a local SQLite catalog
Converting Python agents into Java servlets
questions.why: Per §1.6 & Trigger #20: MCP Toolbox for Databases is Google's open-source MCP server for databases that handles connection pooling, IAM authentication, and observability so you can add DB tools in under 10 lines of code.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.6 Protocols | Tab 3 M1L4
questions.q: What enterprise capabilities do Google-managed MCP servers layer on top of standard open-source MCP?
options: MCP discovery (via Agent Registry), IAM and VPC Service Controls governance, spec-compliant auth, Model Armor scanning, and tracing/audit-log observability
Unlimited free Gemini Pro token usage with no IAM checks
Automatic removal of all system prompts to save context tokens
Direct bypass of VPC Service Controls perimeters
